transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Oliver Chen (Westbridge - Head of AI), Priya Narang (CTO), Samir Gupta (Infra)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery focused on dedicated GPU capacity for Westbridge's internal LLM workloads. Key concerns: isolation/data residency, predictable throughput, burst handling, and cost. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark, technical deep dive.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you all hear me okay?
00:03 Oliver: Yep, good, thanks Maya
00:05 Priya: Hi, yes thanks
00:12 Maya: Quick intros - I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, Daniel our systems engineer is on the line for the deep infra questions
00:18 Daniel: hi all
00:25 Oliver: Oliver, head of AI at Westbridge, we run a mix of internal models, mostly finetuned Llama and some proprietary ranking models
00:35 Priya: Priya, CTO, i'll be involved for security and compliance decisions
00:39 Samir: Samir, infra lead, i deal with networking and provisioning
00:45 Maya: Great, the purpose today is to understand your workloads and see if Dedicated makes sense vs Hosted or Private
01:05 Oliver: high level, we're doing customer support summarization, fraud detection prompts, and internal docs search. Peak is around 120 concurrent users, roughly 3k qps across endpoints during peak, though that number spikes during batch reporting windows
01:25 Daniel: when you say qps is that per model or aggregate across models?
01:30 Oliver: aggregate; the heavy work is the summarization model, longest context 8k tokens, most requests 512 tokens
01:42 Maya: sounds like predictable throughput requirement, isolation / data controls?
01:46 Priya: Yes SOC2 in place, we need audit logs and KMS integration, and for regulatory reasons some PII can't leave our VPC. We're evaluating Dedicated because we want reserved GPUs and customer isolation, maybe Private if needed for full VPC control
02:05 Daniel: for Dedicated, we provide reserved GPU pools in a customer tenant, with network isolation and optional VPC peering for data plane. We also support Private deployments when customers need an on-prem or VPC-hosted control plane
02:20 Samir: can you talk about burst capacity? some of our jobs are spiky, like end of month runs
02:27 Daniel: yes, Dedicated supports burst pools—configurable. You can reserve baseline GPUs and have a burst capacity bucket that can be auto-provisioned. Burst can be across instance types, but the fallback and model variants are important for latency consistency
02:45 Oliver: important for us is latency SLO 95th pct under 500ms for short chat flows, and background batch can be slower. Cost is also a factor
02:58 Maya: got it, we can propose a mix: reserved baseline for steady state and a smaller burst pool you pay for only when used. Also suggestions like quantized model variants for lower cost and warm KV cache to keep latency low
03:15 Priya: what's the onboarding look like, and how long to provision dedicated capacity?
03:20 Daniel: typical lead time 2-4 weeks for Dedicated depending on region and capacity, private on-prem longer. Provisioning is mostly reserved capacity config and network setup. We have a checklist we'll send
03:35 Samir: what's the model support, can we bring our own finetuned Llama variants? any constraints on bitsandquant?
03:42 Daniel: yes, BYOM supported. We recommend certain quantization profiles; some very aggressive quantization may affect quality. We also support sharded KV cache for long context models
03:55 Oliver: what about multi-tenant risk? i.e., noisy neighbors
04:00 Daniel: Dedicated provides tenant isolation at the runtime level; GPUs are in customer pools. Noisy neighbor risk is mostly eliminated for compute; storage and network need proper QoS which we configure
04:15 Priya: encryption at rest and KMS?
04:18 Daniel: yes, KMS integration for keys, support for customer-managed keys and HSM in private
04:25 Maya: Any regulatory certs you need? we have SOC2 Type II, and can provide compliance docs
04:30 Priya: SOC2 is fine but we need the detailed audit log retention policy
04:35 Maya: we'll attach the SOC2 and audit docs, and retention options
04:40 Oliver: questions on failover—if a region loses capacity, do you auto-fail to hosted models?
04:47 Daniel: we have smart routing and fallback policies; you can configure automatic fallback to a hosted model variant or cross-region failover. Tradeoffs are latency and cost
05:15 Samir: curious about autoscaling: do you do vertical scaling (bigger instances) or horizontal (more pods), and what's the cold start latency?
05:25 Daniel: mostly horizontal with sharded model instances; cold starts depend on model size and the runtime caching. For common models with warm cache, we've seen cold start times sub-30s for large models but we recommend warm pools for low-latency
05:45 Oliver: any benchmarking we can run? we want to run a p95 latency test on our prompt set
05:50 Daniel: yes we'll run a benchmark during the POC. We'll need sample prompts, and your peak qps and some synthetic traffic pattern
06:05 Maya: ok next steps: we'll send pricing, a recommended dedicated configuration, the benchmark checklist and SOC2/audit docs
06:15 Priya: timeline — target POC in April, procurement in May
06:20 Oliver: budget question — can you give an estimated monthly cost for baseline 8 GPUs with burst to 16?
06:30 Maya: we'll include an estimate in pricing, ballpark now maybe $XXk/month depending on GPU type and networking
06:38 Samir: last networking question — support for SAML/SSO and IP allowlists for admin console?
06:44 Daniel: yes SSO via SAML, RBAC, and IP allowlists, plus tenant-level audit logs
06:53 Priya: who would own the POC internally? we'll pick a technical PM and Samir will be our lead
07:00 Oliver: good
07:05 Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the items discussed

Recap: Baseline need: steady 8 GPUs for production, burst to ~16 during spikes; 8k token context support; latency target 95th < 500ms for chat; SOC2/KMS/audit logs required. Next: pricing, config, benchmark scheduling.

Links shared: [Dedicated product brief](https://redwood.ai/docs/dedicated), [SOC2 report (redacted)](https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-redacted), benchmark checklist (shared after call)

End of transcript (some transcription artifacts expected).
